input.question: Why did football overtake baseball in popularity in the U.S. during the 1950s and 1960s?
input.ground_truth: One thing that should be established is that until the 60' or so College Football was much more popular then the multiple Pro leagues out there, and thus when many schools had to suspend play during WW2 that accounts for the downturn seen in the 40's. But then when everyone comes back and tons more can go to college on the GI Bill, then all of a sudden you have more players, and more fans, and you see it take off. With more schools competitive, more Bowls popping up, and the spread of more NCAA controlled games showing up on TV. And with more quality players coming out of college the quality of the pro game began to improve, and of course once the AFL and NFL merged and the Superbowl began it was a perfect made for TV event that could drive viewership.

Question: Why did football overtake baseball in popularity in the U.S. during the 1950s and 1960s?

response.prediction:
Okay! Imagine you have two toys: one is a baseball bat and ball, and the other is a tiny football. In the old days, more kids played with the baseball toy. But then, something cool happened with the football toy.

First, TV came into lots of homes. Football games looked really exciting on TV—lots of running, jumping, and big tackles! Kids and families loved watching together. Baseball games took longer and sometimes didn’t look as exciting on TV.

Also, football games happened just once a week, and they were short and full of action. Baseball games took many days and could be slow sometimes. People started to like watching football more because it was faster and more exciting on TV.

So, because of TV and how fun football looked, more and more people started loving football, and it became more popular than baseball in the 1950s and 1960s.
